questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Identify a concurrent power shared by federal and state governments
questions.stem: A transit planner's board notes that both Congress and a state may levy taxes on fuel sold within that state.

options.text: This power is concurrent because both levels may tax within their spheres.
This power is exclusive to Congress because taxation is a federal function.
options.misconception: treats a concurrent power as exclusively federal

options.text: This power is reserved to the states and cannot be shared with Congress.
options.misconception: treats a concurrent power as exclusively state power

options.text: This power is prohibited to both levels by the Tenth Amendment.
options.misconception: misreads the Tenth Amendment as a prohibition

questions.explanation: Taxation is a concurrent power shared by federal and state governments, so both may levy taxes within their spheres. The tempting error is to treat taxation as belonging to only one level.
questions.hint: Ask whether both levels may tax.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize an exclusive federal power over money

options.misconception: assumes states share the money power

options.text: States may coin money if Congress gives permission by statute.
options.misconception: treats an exclusive power as delegable

options.text: Only the federal government may coin money and regulate its value.
Both levels coin money but states must use federal denominations.
options.misconception: confuses shared currency with shared power

questions.explanation: Coining money is an exclusive federal power, so states cannot issue currency. The tempting error is to assume states retain a residual money power.

questions.explanation: The spending power lets Congress appropriate funds for the general welfare, subject to constitutional limits. The tempting error is to confuse spending with direct regulation of state conduct.

Only the largest account is cut.
Every eligible account is cut by the same percentage automatically.
No cut occurs without a new vote.

questions.explanation: Automatic reductions apply the same percentage to every eligible account. The tempting error is to assume cuts are discretionary or targeted.

options.text: The guaranteed amount is 100000 dollars.

answer.exemplar: Reaching the borrowing limit halts new borrowing until Congress acts, forcing spending delays or payment prioritisation even though existing obligations remain.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Identify a shared-standard model

stimulus.body: Congress sets a common transit safety standard but leaves enforcement and funding administration to each state agency. The board asks how this arrangement works.

questions.stem: Which model does this describe?

options.text: The standard is a federal mandate with no state role.
The standard is purely voluntary guidance.
It is cooperative federalism with a shared standard.
States set the standard and Congress merely funds it.

questions.explanation: A shared standard with state administration is cooperative federalism. The tempting error is to assume pure federal or pure state control.

questions.topic: Authority and money as separate steps
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish authority from appropriation
questions.stem: The board separates a transit programme's authorising statute from its funding.

answer.exemplar: Authorising authority creates the programme and sets its rules, while appropriating money provides the funds, so a programme can exist on paper without any dollars attached.

stimulus.body: A federal transit grant covers capital costs while requiring the state to fund all ongoing operations and maintenance. The board must decide who ultimately bears the cost.
